transcript: Last night my friend Bella and I saw Swing State at the Manedalayan Theater in the West Village. This one act play is set about a year and a half into the COVID 19 pandemic and mostly focuses on a woman named Pegg in her Wisconsin farmhouse. Pegg's husband died about a year ago, and now her only regular companion is Ryan, a local ex convict who she looks out for. The plot largely revolves around a gun that goes missing, but it's more just a device for us to learn about pegs and Ryan's relationship and their mental states. I felt like the play was about loss, grief, codependency, and how, as pegs says at one point, you can't give up even if you want to. I thought it was really well acted, but in retrospect, I think the structure of the play was too predictable, too carefully constructed, with too many expositional backstories which would only happen out of necessity for the audience as opposed to what would be natural for the characters. But regardless, I think this was still a really solid portrait of this moment where people are still grappling with loss and still languishing in this era of instability. With that, another play Bill for my collection.
reasoning: Creator praises acting and thematic resonance but criticizes predictable structure and forced exposition. Lands as a thoughtful mixed-to-mildly-positive take without a clear recommendation.
